## Final Trading Report

### Account Summary
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Starting equity | $16.82 |
| Ending equity | $16.47 |

### Trade Count
- **27 orders submitted** (nonces 95-121)
- **26 filled**, 1 expired (SHIN-ETSU — wide spread, limit never hit)
- **13 round trips** (open + close)

### Markets Traded
0700-HK/USD, SMIC/USD, Hua Hong/USD, BYD/USD, ANT/USD, Xiaomi/1810-HK, KUAISHOU/USD, META/USD, AMZN/USD, SHIN-ETSU/USD (expired)

### What Went Wrong

1. **Spread friction was the killer.** Every round trip paid the bid-ask spread twice (enter + exit) plus 0.045% taker fee each way. With typical spreads of 0.1-0.5%, each $5 round trip cost $0.01-0.03 in pure friction. Over 13 round trips that's about $0.26 — almost all of the loss.

2. **No close was profitable.** Every single close realized a loss. Even when mark-to-market showed a profit (e.g. Hua Hong was +$0.03 unrealized), the actual close ate the profit because the fill crossed the spread to the other side of the book.

3. **Oracle convergence was too slow for scalping.** The strategy of shorting when price > oracle was directionally correct (most markets were above oracle), but the convergence played out over minutes to hours, not seconds. Rapid rotation traded away the edge before it paid.

4. **LONG trades consistently lost.** Both SMIC longs went against me. The market had a persistent upward bias (prices above oracle), making mean-reversion longs the wrong side.

### What Worked
- **Short bias was correct** — prices were consistently above oracle across the board
- **Tight-spread markets** (0700-HK, Xiaomi) had the best in-trade P&L
- **KUAISHOU** was the best unrealized position (+$0.01) before close

### Lesson
On pod's batch-auction order books with ~0.2% spreads and 0.045% taker fees, a scalping strategy that rotates every 1-2 minutes loses money to friction. A profitable approach would need either (a) maker-only orders (POST_ONLY) to avoid taker fees and get fills inside the spread, or (b) longer holds to let convergence outweigh the two spread crossings.
